_summary.generator: Blitzy cross-layer synthesis pipeline (normalize -> merge -> corroborate -> gate)
_summary.corroborationCriterion: Location-anchored cross-layer corroboration: a finding is corroborated only when two or more DIFFERENT layers report a finding at the exact same file:line. Confidence is 'high' when the matched layers also share a CWE at that location and 'medium' for same-file:line matches without CWE overlap. Same-file-only (different line) and repository-wide CWE-theme matches are explicitly excluded. Each corroborated finding exposes clusterSeverity/maxSeverity = the maximum severity across its location cluster so corroboration never masks a higher-severity match from another layer.

_summary.note: Single cross-correlated merged report (Directives 8 & 9), synthesized only from the four per-layer normalized JSON artifacts under one unified severity vocabulary (critical/high/medium/low). Cross-layer corroboration is location-anchored: findings are corroborated only when >=2 distinct layers flag the exact same file:line (high confidence when they also share a CWE at that location, medium otherwise); same-file-only and repository-wide CWE-theme matches are excluded, and every corroborated finding carries clusterSeverity/maxSeverity = the cluster maximum so corroboration cannot mask a higher-severity match. The gate verdict is a precedence fold ERROR>BLOCK>WARN>PASS; a failed layer never silently passes. All severity counts equal the sum of the per-layer normalized findings. These figures are the canonical numbers reused by security-audit-decision-log.md and security-audit-executive-presentation.html.

findings.title: Legacy symmetric encryption uses unauthenticated AES-256-CBC
findings.description: symmetricEncrypt/symmetricDecrypt use ALGORITHM="aes256" (Node alias for AES-256-CBC), an unauthenticated cipher mode. CBC ciphertext is malleable and provides no integrity, exposing the legacy credential-encryption path to bit-flipping and padding-oracle style attacks if ciphertext is ever attacker-influenced. No MAC/auth tag accompanies the ciphertext format `iv:ciphertext`.
findings.recommendation: Prefer the authenticated AES-256-GCM keyring (packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts) for all new secrets and plan a backward-compatible migration of legacy CBC values; do not change the in-use key or format in this audit.
findings.demotionReason: A random per-message IV is generated (packages/lib/crypto.ts:17) and the modern authenticated AES-256-GCM keyring already exists for new secrets; the legacy CBC path is retained under the platform's encryption-key-continuity hard constraint and is not directly fed attacker-controlled ciphertext.
findings.message: Legacy symmetric encryption uses unauthenticated AES-256-CBC

findings.title: Encryption key consumed as a raw Latin1 buffer without a key-derivation function
findings.description: The key is materialized with Buffer.from(key, "latin1") in both symmetricEncrypt (line 16) and symmetricDecrypt (line 32). CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is therefore used verbatim as raw key bytes with no KDF (PBKDF2/HKDF/scrypt) and no salt; key strength depends entirely on operator-supplied entropy, and Latin1 decoding silently truncates/maps multibyte input rather than rejecting an out-of-spec key length.
findings.recommendation: Derive a fixed-length key via HKDF/scrypt from the configured secret and validate key length at startup; keep the current key value unchanged (encryption-key continuity is a hard constraint).
findings.demotionReason: Deployment docs require a 32-byte CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY and the newer keyring validates key length explicitly (packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts:67-70, base64url 32-byte keys); the value cannot be rotated in this detection-only engagement.
findings.message: Encryption key consumed as a raw Latin1 buffer without a key-derivation function

findings.title: AES-256-GCM decryption omits explicit authTagLength hardening
findings.description: createDecipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, nonce) is called without the { authTagLength: 16 } option. While the auth tag is still validated via setAuthTag, not pinning the tag length is a defense-in-depth gap that a truncated-tag forgery attempt could probe.
findings.recommendation: Pass { authTagLength: 16 } to createDecipheriv (and createCipheriv) to pin GCM tag length explicitly.
findings.demotionReason: GCM remains authenticated and the 16-byte tag produced by getAuthTag is enforced via setAuthTag; the default tag length already matches, so exposure is theoretical.
findings.message: AES-256-GCM decryption omits explicit authTagLength hardening

findings.title: Magic-link email token lifetime is 10 hours despite a comment stating 10 minutes
findings.description: The NextAuth EmailProvider sets maxAge: 10 * 60 * 60 (36000 seconds = 10 hours) while the adjacent comment reads "Magic links are valid for 10 min only". The effective passwordless sign-in window is two orders of magnitude larger than intended, widening the interception/replay window for emailed verification links.
findings.recommendation: Align the maxAge with the documented intent (e.g. 10 * 60 for 10 minutes) and add a test asserting the magic-link TTL.
findings.demotionReason: Verification tokens are single-use and bound to email delivery, and NextAuth invalidates the token on first successful use; the issue is an over-long lifetime rather than a missing control.
findings.message: Magic-link email token lifetime is 10 hours despite a comment stating 10 minutes

findings.title: Stateless JWT sessions have no server-side revocation; logout only deletes the cookie
findings.description: session.strategy is "jwt", so sessions are stateless bearer tokens. Logout deletes the next-auth.session-token cookie at the edge (apps/web/proxy.ts:101) but a previously issued JWT remains valid until expiry, so a captured token cannot be centrally revoked before maxAge elapses.
findings.recommendation: Consider short JWT lifetimes plus a server-side denylist or rotating session version claim for high-assurance logout/force-revocation flows.
findings.demotionReason: Per-user sessionTimeout shortens maxAge during JWT encode (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:527) and cookies are issued Secure/HttpOnly via defaultCookies(https) (line 534); stateless JWT is an intentional, widely accepted NextAuth design.
findings.message: Stateless JWT sessions have no server-side revocation; logout only deletes the cookie

findings.title: Enforced Content-Security-Policy is applied only to login routes
findings.description: shouldEnforceCsp returns true only for paths starting with /auth/login or /login (apps/web/proxy.ts:64-66). Because getCspHeader emits no header when enforcement is off (apps/web/lib/csp.ts:44-51), the nonce-based CSP that mitigates XSS is absent on the vast majority of authenticated application pages.
findings.recommendation: Roll out the nonce-based enforced CSP across all app routes (not just login) once streaming-script nonce coverage is complete; until then, track the gap explicitly.
findings.demotionReason: A nonce + strict-dynamic CSP is fully implemented for the highest-risk credential-entry pages, and React's default output escaping plus server-side input validation provide baseline XSS defense elsewhere.
findings.message: Enforced Content-Security-Policy is applied only to login routes

findings.title: Development CSP enables 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'
findings.description: In the non-production branch, script-src resolves to "'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https: http:", disabling script-source restrictions during development.
findings.recommendation: Keep the relaxed policy strictly behind the IS_PRODUCTION guard (as implemented) and avoid shipping any build that evaluates the dev branch.
findings.demotionReason: The relaxed directives are gated by IS_PRODUCTION; production uses 'nonce-<n>' 'strict-dynamic' (apps/web/lib/csp.ts:22), so the weakness does not reach production traffic.
findings.message: Development CSP enables 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'

findings.title: style-src permits 'unsafe-inline' in non-strict and development policies
findings.description: style-src includes 'unsafe-inline' whenever CSP_POLICY="non-strict" or in development, allowing inline style injection (a lower-impact CSS-based vector) on those configurations.
findings.recommendation: Adopt nonces/hashes for inline styles so 'unsafe-inline' can be removed from style-src even in non-strict mode.
findings.demotionReason: Default production policy omits 'unsafe-inline' for style-src (empty string at line 30), and CSS injection carries materially lower impact than script injection.
findings.message: style-src permits 'unsafe-inline' in non-strict and development policies

findings.title: Rate-limit IP derivation trusts the client-supplied cf-connecting-ip header first
findings.description: Both handleRequest (line 57) and getTracker (line 215) resolve the client IP as request.headers["cf-connecting-ip"] ?? request.headers["CF-Connecting-IP"] ?? request.ip. If the API is reachable without strictly terminating behind Cloudflare, a client can spoof cf-connecting-ip to rotate its rate-limit identity and bypass IP-based throttling.
findings.recommendation: Only trust cf-connecting-ip when the connecting peer is a verified Cloudflare egress IP; otherwise fall back to the socket address (request.ip).
findings.demotionReason: Authenticated requests are tracked by SHA-256 hash of the API key / access token / OAuth client BEFORE the IP fallback (apps/api/v2/src/lib/throttler-guard.ts:217-228), so IP spoofing only affects anonymous traffic; the canonical deployment fronts the API with Cloudflare.
findings.message: Rate-limit IP derivation trusts the client-supplied cf-connecting-ip header first

findings.title: Open-redirect surface: edge middleware redirects to an unvalidated return-to cookie
findings.description: On /apps/installed the middleware reads the return-to cookie and issues NextResponse.redirect(new URL(returnTo.value, req.url)). Because new URL() honours an absolute URL in the first argument, a return-to value such as https://evil.example overrides the base origin, yielding an open redirect if the cookie can be planted (e.g. via an earlier injection or subdomain).
findings.recommendation: Validate that the resolved redirect target is same-origin (or matches an allowlist) before redirecting; reject or strip absolute external URLs.
findings.demotionReason: The redirect target comes from a cookie rather than a directly attacker-supplied query parameter, requiring a prior write primitive, and the cookie is deleted immediately after use (apps/web/proxy.ts:89).
findings.message: Open-redirect surface: edge middleware redirects to an unvalidated return-to cookie

findings.title: API v1 security middleware is opt-in per route rather than globally enforced
findings.description: The legacy API composes auth and throttling through next-api-middleware labels (middlewareOrder: extendRequest, captureErrors, verifyApiKey, rateLimitApiKey, addRequestId, captureUserId) that each route must explicitly apply. Across ~82 file-based handlers, any route that forgets to wrap itself with verifyApiKey/rateLimitApiKey ships unauthenticated or unthrottled, with no framework-level backstop.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a default-deny wrapper or lint/test that asserts every public v1 route applies the auth + rate-limit middleware chain.
findings.demotionReason: A shared withMiddleware helper standardizes ordering and is consistently applied across the v1 route set, and verifyApiKey + rateLimitApiKey unit tests exist alongside the helpers.
findings.message: API v1 security middleware is opt-in per route rather than globally enforced

findings.title: Broad log-injection surface from request-derived values written to logs
findings.description: Request handling logs request-derived context across the API and packages; unsanitized user-controlled values flowing into log lines enable log forging/injection (CRLF, fake entries) and can poison downstream log analysis. This is an architecture-wide observation seeded by the Layer 3a inventory rather than a single line.
findings.recommendation: Centralize logging through a structured logger that encodes/escapes user-controlled fields and strips CR/LF before emission.
findings.demotionReason: Logging is funneled through structured logger utilities and request-id correlation (addRequestid.ts), limiting free-form string concatenation; impact is integrity-of-logs rather than direct code execution.
findings.message: Broad log-injection surface from request-derived values written to logs

findings.title: Dockerfile defines default build-time secret values for auth and encryption keys
findings.description: ARG NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret (line 11) and ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret (line 12) provide weak default values that are promoted into ENV (lines 29-30) and consumed by the Next.js build. If an image is built without overriding these args, the resulting artifact is associated with the predictable value "secret", and the defaults invite copy-paste into real deployments.
findings.recommendation: Remove the insecure defaults and fail the build when NEXTAUTH_SECRET / CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY are unset, forcing explicit secure values; inject real secrets only at runtime.
findings.demotionReason: These are build-time ARGs needed for the Next.js compile step rather than runtime secrets; production deployments inject real values at runtime (docker-compose passes them through, and start.sh re-templates), so the default does not necessarily reach a running instance.
findings.message: Dockerfile defines default build-time secret values for auth and encryption keys

findings.title: Container image runs as root (no USER directive)
findings.description: None of the build/runner stages declare a USER, so the final image starts the application as root (CMD scripts/start.sh at line 94). A container compromise therefore begins with root in the container, increasing blast radius if combined with a kernel or runtime escape.
findings.recommendation: Create and switch to a non-root user (USER node) for the runner stage and ensure file ownership/permissions are compatible.
findings.demotionReason: Production orchestration commonly enforces runAsNonRoot/securityContext at the platform layer, and a HEALTHCHECK is defined (Dockerfile:91-92); this is a hardening gap rather than an exploitable flaw on its own.
findings.message: Container image runs as root (no USER directive)

findings.title: GitHub Actions workflows contain shell-injection-prone run steps
findings.description: Semgrep flags run: steps that interpolate context expressions directly into the shell across three locations (release-docker.yaml:53, cubic-devin-review-trigger.yml:18, actions/docker-build-and-test/action.yml:121). Untrusted interpolated values (e.g. PR-derived fields) embedded in run scripts can lead to command injection in CI with access to repository secrets.
findings.recommendation: Move interpolated values into env: bindings and reference them as "$VAR" in run steps; never inline ${{ github.event.* }} directly into shell commands.
findings.demotionReason: Exploitation requires an interpolated value to be attacker-controllable for the specific step; several occurrences interpolate trusted release/tag context rather than untrusted PR input.
findings.message: GitHub Actions workflows contain shell-injection-prone run steps

findings.title: pull_request_target workflows check out PR-controlled refs
findings.description: Six workflows trigger on pull_request_target (which runs with the base repository's write-scoped token and secrets). At least devin-conflict-resolver.yml (checkout @ line 221, operating on pr.head_ref) and stale-pr-devin-completion.yml (checkout @ line 145) check out PR-controlled branches under that trigger, the classic pattern that can leak the privileged token / secrets to untrusted PR code.
findings.recommendation: Avoid checking out and executing untrusted PR code under pull_request_target; prefer the workflow_run pattern or pin to the base ref and gate any PR-code execution behind manual approval.
findings.demotionReason: devin-conflict-resolver.yml is gated by a maintainer-applied label (line 23) and several pull_request_target workflows only orchestrate/dispatch the real CI via head_sha (run-ci.yml) rather than executing PR code with secrets.
findings.message: pull_request_target workflows check out PR-controlled refs

findings.title: docker-compose ships hardcoded default database credentials
findings.description: The compose database service hardcodes POSTGRES_USER=unicorn_user and POSTGRES_PASSWORD=magical_password (lines 20-21). If reused beyond local development, these well-known defaults expose the database.
findings.recommendation: Source database credentials from environment variables / secrets and document that the compose file is for local development only.
findings.demotionReason: docker-compose.yml is a local-development convenience stack (not the production deployment manifest) and the credentials are illustrative placeholders.
findings.message: docker-compose ships hardcoded default database credentials

findings.title: Outbound webhooks are sent unsigned when no subscriber secret is configured
findings.description: createWebhookSignature returns "" when params.secret is falsy (line 350), and _sendPayload only sets the X-Cal-Signature-256 header when the signature is truthy (lines 369-370). A subscriber that did not configure a secret therefore receives an unsigned POST, so it cannot verify payload authenticity/integrity and may act on a spoofed delivery.
findings.recommendation: Warn or block on creation of webhook subscriptions without a secret, and document that unsigned delivery offers no authenticity guarantee.
findings.demotionReason: When a secret is present, payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 (packages/features/webhooks/lib/sendPayload.ts:349); the unsigned path is an opt-in of the subscriber, not a verification bypass on inbound traffic.
findings.message: Outbound webhooks are sent unsigned when no subscriber secret is configured

findings.title: Inbound Vercel webhook verification uses the deprecated HMAC-SHA1 construction
findings.description: VercelWebhookGuard computes crypto.createHmac("sha1", webhookSecret) (line 44) to verify the x-vercel-signature header. SHA-1 is deprecated for collision resistance, and although HMAC-SHA1 remains a sound MAC, the algorithm choice is a hygiene concern.
findings.recommendation: Where the provider supports it, migrate to HMAC-SHA256; otherwise document that SHA-1 is mandated by the Vercel signature contract.
findings.demotionReason: HMAC-SHA1 has no practical forgery against MAC usage, the comparison is constant-time via crypto.timingSafeEqual (apps/api/v2/src/vercel-webhook.guard.ts:53-56), and the SHA-1 format is dictated by Vercel's external webhook contract.
findings.message: Inbound Vercel webhook verification uses the deprecated HMAC-SHA1 construction

findings.title: Input validation is globally enforced in API v2 but only per-route in API v1
findings.description: API v2 installs a global ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, transform: true }) (bootstrap.ts:71-83) that strips unknown properties on every DTO. API v1 instead relies on per-route Zod parsing, so any v1 handler that forgets to validate its body/query accepts arbitrary unvalidated input, creating an enforcement asymmetry across the two APIs.
findings.recommendation: Standardize a v1 validation wrapper (or shared schema-first handler factory) so body/query validation is structurally guaranteed, matching the v2 global pipe.
findings.demotionReason: Zod schemas are widely used across apps/api/v1/lib/validations and payloads are validated with safeParse at trust boundaries (e.g. packages/app-store/btcpayserver/api/webhook.ts:54), limiting the practical gap.
findings.message: Input validation is globally enforced in API v2 but only per-route in API v1

findings.title: Type-confusion surface from parsing untrusted JSON/structured input
findings.description: The Layer 3a inventory enumerates a large CWE-843 (type confusion) surface where untrusted input is parsed and consumed; without strict schema coercion at every boundary, mismatched types can bypass downstream assumptions.
findings.recommendation: Ensure every external input boundary uses strict schema validation/coercion (Zod/class-validator) before the value is used.
findings.demotionReason: The v2 ValidationPipe transforms and whitelists DTOs and v1 uses Zod safeParse at boundaries, so most parse sites already coerce types; residual risk is in any unguarded boundary.
findings.message: Type-confusion surface from parsing untrusted JSON/structured input

findings.title: Parent-to-iframe postMessage uses a wildcard ('*') targetOrigin
findings.description: doInIframe posts commands to the embedded iframe with targetOrigin "*" (embed.ts:409-411), acknowledged by the in-code TODO at line 407. If the iframe is ever navigated to an unexpected origin, those command messages (method/arg) are delivered to that origin, leaking embed command context cross-origin.
findings.recommendation: Derive targetOrigin from the configured embed origin (__config.origin) and pass it explicitly instead of "*".
findings.demotionReason: The messages carry non-sensitive UI commands tagged originator:"CAL", and in practice the iframe is the operator's own cal.com origin; no credentials or tokens traverse this channel.
findings.message: Parent-to-iframe postMessage uses a wildcard ('*') targetOrigin

findings.title: Parent message listener fires SDK actions without validating event.origin
findings.description: The global window message handler (embed.ts:1597-1614) reads e.data and dispatches actionManager.fire(...) based solely on the message's fullType, without checking e.origin. Any frame/window able to post a well-formed message can trigger embed SDK actions in the host page.
findings.recommendation: Validate e.origin against the configured embed origin allowlist before processing inbound messages.
findings.demotionReason: Dispatched actions are client-side UI events (resize, link-ready, error surfacing) routed through namespaced actionManagers with no privileged/server-side effect, bounding the blast radius.
findings.message: Parent message listener fires SDK actions without validating event.origin

findings.title: API v1 accepts the API key via URL query parameter while v2 uses an Authorization header
findings.description: Legacy v1 reads the key from req.query.apiKey (verifyApiKey.ts:25,27 and rateLimitApiKey.ts:9), so secrets land in URLs and are routinely captured by access logs, proxies, and browser history. API v2 instead takes an Authorization: Bearer header, a divergence that weakens the v1 surface.
findings.recommendation: Accept the v1 key via Authorization header (deprecating the query parameter) to match v2 and avoid secret leakage through URL logging.
findings.demotionReason: Keys are SHA-256 hashed before lookup (verifyApiKey.ts:28) so logs never contain the stored secret form, and transport is HTTPS; the query-parameter form is retained for backward compatibility.
findings.message: API v1 accepts the API key via URL query parameter while v2 uses an Authorization header

findings.title: Divergent enforcement models: per-route middleware (v1) vs global guards (v2)
findings.description: v2 enforces auth/validation/throttling globally (ValidationPipe + ~15 guard folders under apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/guards), whereas v1 depends on each route opting into withMiddleware. The two surfaces can drift, so a protection present in v2 may be silently absent on the analogous v1 endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Document a parity matrix of controls across v1/v2 and converge toward default-enforced protection in v1.
findings.demotionReason: Both APIs implement authentication and rate limiting; the difference is enforcement mechanism, not absence of controls, and v1's shared middleware helper standardizes the chain.
findings.message: Divergent enforcement models: per-route middleware (v1) vs global guards (v2)

findings.title: Rate-limiting algorithms differ between v1 (per-user) and v2 (per-credential/IP with DB limits)
findings.description: v1 throttles by numeric userId (rateLimitApiKey.ts:13) via checkRateLimitAndThrowError, while v2 throttles by SHA-256 hash of API key/access token/OAuth client (falling back to IP) with per-key DB-configured limits. The divergent identity and limit models make consistent quota enforcement across versions difficult to reason about.
findings.recommendation: Define a shared rate-limit policy/specification and align identifiers and default limits across v1 and v2.
findings.demotionReason: Both versions enforce rate limits and emit X-RateLimit-* headers, and @unkey/ratelimit underpins limiting; the divergence is an operational-consistency concern, not a missing control.
findings.message: Rate-limiting algorithms differ between v1 (per-user) and v2 (per-credential/IP with DB limits)

findings.title: Committed CRON_API_KEY default in .env.example guards 10+ sensitive cron routes
findings.description: The committed environment template sets CRON_API_KEY to a fixed 32-hex literal value (redacted here as 0cc0e6**REDACTED**) that authorizes 10+ App Router cron endpoints (e.g. apps/web/app/api/cron/downgradeUsers, /credentials, /changeTimeZone, /webhookTriggers). Because the value is public in the repository, any deployment that does not override it exposes privileged maintenance operations to anyone who replays the well-known key.
findings.recommendation: Remove the literal value from the committed template (leave CRON_API_KEY= blank like NEXTAUTH_SECRET), require operators to generate a unique key, and rotate any environment that adopted the default.
findings.demotionReason: The value lives in .env.example (a template), not in a committed live .env, and production deployments are expected to set their own CRON_API_KEY; the cron handlers do enforce the key before acting.
findings.message: Committed CRON_API_KEY default in .env.example guards 10+ sensitive cron routes

findings.title: Cron endpoint authorization uses a non-constant-time comparison and accepts the key via query string
findings.description: Representative cron handlers read the secret as request.headers.get("authorization") || searchParams.get("apiKey") (line 14) and authorize with a plain process.env.CRON_API_KEY !== apiKey comparison (line 16). The query-parameter acceptance leaks the secret into URL logs, and the !== comparison is not constant-time, exposing a timing side-channel on the secret.
findings.recommendation: Compare the cron secret with crypto.timingSafeEqual and accept it only via the Authorization header (drop the apiKey query parameter).
findings.demotionReason: The cron secret is a high-entropy 32-hex token, making a network-observable timing attack impractical, and transport is HTTPS; the comparison gates a non-interactive maintenance endpoint rather than user auth.
findings.message: Cron endpoint authorization uses a non-constant-time comparison and accepts the key via query string

findings.title: Multiple dangerouslySetInnerHTML usages create a React XSS sink surface
findings.description: Semgrep identifies nine dangerouslySetInnerHTML usages across apps/web (e.g. EventTypeDescription.tsx:63, slug-view.tsx:71, team-view.tsx:161, users-public-view.tsx:108). Each is a potential stored/reflected XSS sink if the injected HTML derives from user-controllable content without robust sanitization.
findings.recommendation: Audit each usage to confirm the HTML is constant or sanitized (e.g. DOMPurify) and replace with safe rendering where the source is user-controlled.
findings.demotionReason: React escapes all default output and these are a small, enumerable set of intentional rich-text/markdown render points typically fed sanitized or trusted content; this is a surface to verify, not a confirmed injection.
findings.message: Multiple dangerouslySetInnerHTML usages create a React XSS sink surface

Instead, use an intermediate environment variable with `env:` to store the data and use the environment variable in the `run:` script. Be sure to use double-quotes the environment variable, like this: "$ENVVAR".

OAuth authorize redirect to client-supplied redirect_uri
findings.message: body.redirectUri flows into res.redirect(`${body.redirectUri}?code=${id}`). The authorization code is appended to a user-supplied URL, an open-redirect / code-leak sink.
findings.recommendation: Keep the strict redirect_uri allowlist; prefer exact-match comparison over prefix/origin matching.
findings.demotionReason: redirect_uri is validated against the registered client allowlist via isOriginAllowed(body.redirectUri, oauthClient.redirectUris) at oauth-flow.controller.ts:67, which throws BadRequestException before the redirect; only pre-registered origins are reachable.

findings.title: Docs redirect target sourced from environment variable
findings.message: res.redirect(process.env.DOCS_URL) on /docs paths. The destination is a server-controlled environment variable, not request input.
findings.recommendation: No action required; optionally validate DOCS_URL is an absolute https URL at boot.
findings.demotionReason: Redirect target is read from server-side process.env.DOCS_URL and is not attacker-controllable; the path predicate only gates which requests redirect, not the destination.

findings.title: Conferencing OAuth returnTo propagated into post-auth redirect
findings.message: @Query('returnTo') is carried as `returnTo: returnTo ?? origin` through the OAuth state and used as the post-connect redirect destination.
findings.recommendation: Validate returnTo against an allowlist of first-party paths/origins before redirecting.
findings.demotionReason: returnTo is round-tripped through the provider OAuth `state` and defaulted to the request origin; the connect flow requires an authenticated session, limiting practical phishing value.

findings.title: OAuth2 exception filter performs 303 redirect to exception-supplied URL
findings.message: response.redirect(303, exception.redirectUrl) sends the client to a URL carried on a thrown OAuth2RedirectException.
findings.recommendation: Ensure every throw site populates redirectUrl from a validated/registered client redirect URI.
findings.demotionReason: redirectUrl is set by server-side OAuth2 flow code that constructs the exception, not directly from raw request input; values originate from validated client configuration.

findings.title: Stripe connect returnTo used as redirect destination
findings.message: @Query('returnTo') flows into `returnTo: !!returnTo ? returnTo : origin` and is later used to redirect the user after the Stripe connect round-trip.
findings.recommendation: Constrain returnTo to a first-party allowlist before issuing the redirect.
findings.demotionReason: returnTo is encoded into the Stripe OAuth `state` and defaulted to the request origin; the endpoint requires an authenticated org/user context.

findings.title: Outbound webhook delivery fetches a fully user-configured URL with no egress allowlist
findings.message: subscriberUrl (configured by an authenticated user with webhook-management permission) flows directly into fetch(subscriberUrl, {method:'POST', body}). There is no destination allowlist or private/link-local IP filtering, so a tenant can target internal services or cloud metadata (e.g. 169.254.169.254), yielding authenticated SSRF.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and validate subscriberUrl against a deny-list of private/link-local/loopback ranges (or an allowlist), block DNS-rebinding by pinning the resolved IP, and keep redirect:'manual' (already set) to prevent redirect-based pivots.

findings.title: Logo proxy fetches a request-influenced logo URL
findings.message: response = await fetch(filteredLogo) issues a server-side request to a logo URL derived from request parameters.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the filter rejects non-allowlisted hosts and private IP ranges; add explicit SSRF guard on the resolved address.
findings.demotionReason: The variable name and flow indicate the value is pre-filtered ('filteredLogo') against the known app-store logo definitions before fetch; arbitrary external hosts are not directly reachable from raw input.

findings.title: Vercel webhook handler performs an outbound fetch to a payload-derived URL
findings.message: const response = await fetch(url, {...}) where url is derived from the inbound webhook payload.
findings.recommendation: Additionally constrain the fetched URL to Vercel API hosts.
findings.demotionReason: The endpoint is signature-verified by vercel-webhook.guard using crypto.timingSafeEqual (constant-time HMAC check at vercel-webhook.guard.ts:53), so only Vercel-originated, integrity-checked payloads reach the fetch.

findings.title: License check fetches a server-configured license endpoint
findings.message: const response = await fetch(licenseKeyUrl, { mode: 'cors' }) calls the licensing service.
findings.recommendation: Pin the license host; no user-facing remediation required.
findings.demotionReason: licenseKeyUrl is a server-side configured constant (license service base URL), not user-controllable input.

findings.title: Office365 token exchange uses a hard-coded Microsoft endpoint
findings.message: await fetch('https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token', ...) is a fixed, trusted destination.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The fetch target is a string literal pointing at the Microsoft identity platform; no user input contributes to the host.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.sinkText: this.logger.error(`Booking with uid=${booking.uid} has no host`);
findings.title: Booking uid interpolated into an error log line
findings.message: this.logger.error(`Booking with uid=${booking.uid} has no host`) interpolates a booking identifier into a log message.
findings.recommendation: Prefer passing dynamic values as structured metadata (second argument) rather than string interpolation.
findings.demotionReason: booking.uid is a server-generated CUID-style identifier (not free-form user text), and the structured logger escapes control characters; CRLF log-forging is not practically reachable.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.title: Booking request context logged at creation
findings.message: this.logger.log(`createBookingRequest_2024_08_13`, {...}) records request context for a booking create.
findings.recommendation: Continue logging request data as structured fields; redact PII where present.
findings.demotionReason: The dynamic data is passed as a structured metadata object (second argument), not concatenated into the message string, so newline/control-character injection into the log line is prevented.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.sinkText: this.logger.error(`Failed to load default calendars of user with id: ${userId}`, {
findings.title: User id interpolated into a calendar processor error log
findings.message: this.logger.error(`Failed to load default calendars of user with id: ${userId}`, {...}).
findings.recommendation: Pass userId as structured metadata for consistency.
findings.demotionReason: userId is a numeric primary key; non-numeric/CRLF content cannot reach this interpolation, so log forging is infeasible.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.title: Exception message interpolated into the global HTTP exception log
findings.message: this.logger.error(`Http Exception Filter: ${exception?.message}`, {...}) may include text that originated from request-derived validation errors.
findings.recommendation: Encode/strip CR/LF from interpolated exception messages before logging to fully eliminate log-forging risk.
findings.demotionReason: Messages come from server-thrown HttpException instances (controlled strings / validation summaries), not raw request bodies; the structured logger neutralizes control characters in the rendered line.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.sinkText: console.error(`Error: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error occurred"}`);
findings.title: Startup script prints caught error to stderr
findings.message: console.error(`Error: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error occurred'}`) runs in the container start script.
findings.recommendation: No action required for this build/ops script.
findings.demotionReason: Executes only at container startup with no untrusted request input in scope; not reachable from the running application's request surface.

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.title: API authentication derives identity from req.query.apiKey
findings.message: strippedApiKey = `${req.query.apiKey}`.replace(prefix,'') feeds the API-key auth decision, and the key travels in the URL query string.
findings.recommendation: Accept the API key via Authorization header rather than the query string to avoid leakage into access logs/referrers.
findings.demotionReason: The key is hashed with hashAPIKey (SHA-256) and matched against the stored hash via ApiKeyService.verifyKeyByHashedKey; identity is established cryptographically, and isAdminGuard + isLockedOrBlocked run afterward (verifyApiKey.ts:44-48).

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.sinkText: if (!req.query.apiKey) return res.status(401).json({ message: "No apiKey provided" });
findings.title: Presence check on req.query.apiKey gates the request
findings.message: if (!req.query.apiKey) returns 401; the raw query parameter is the entry point of the auth decision.
findings.recommendation: Move the credential to the Authorization header.
findings.demotionReason: This is only a presence guard; the actual trust decision uses the SHA-256 hash comparison against the persisted key (api-key-hashing mitigation), so the untrusted value never short-circuits authorization on its own.

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.title: Credential-sync secret compared from a request header
findings.message: req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-credential-sync-secret'] is read and compared to the configured secret to authorize credential sync.
findings.recommendation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual for the secret comparison to remove the timing side-channel (CWE-208).
findings.demotionReason: The header value is compared against a server-side environment secret (CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_SECRET); the feature is additionally disabled unless explicitly enabled, bounding exposure.

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.sinkText: const nextAuthToken = await getToken({ req: request, secret: nextAuthSecret });
findings.title: NextAuth token extracted from the request for the auth strategy
findings.message: const nextAuthToken = await getToken({ req: request, secret: nextAuthSecret }) reads the session token from the incoming request.
findings.recommendation: No action required; ensure NEXTAUTH_SECRET rotation policy is documented.
findings.demotionReason: getToken cryptographically verifies the JWT/session token using the server-side NEXTAUTH_SECRET; a forged or tampered token fails verification and yields null, so the untrusted request cannot dictate identity.

findings.title: Math.random used to build a short non-secret identifier suffix
findings.message: return Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 10) produces a short token-like string.
findings.recommendation: If this value ever guards access, switch to crypto.randomBytes; otherwise no action required.
findings.demotionReason: The value is used as a non-security display/slug identifier, not as a session token, password-reset token, or API key; all credential/token generation in the codebase uses crypto.randomBytes/getRandomValues.

findings.title: Math.random used for non-security jitter value
findings.message: const getRandomness = () => Number(Math.random().toFixed(3)) generates a small fractional value.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Used for scheduling/display jitter, not for any cryptographic or authorization purpose.

findings.title: Math.random drives loading-skeleton bar heights
findings.message: style={{ height: `${Math.random() * 40 + 30}%` }} randomizes a UI skeleton placeholder.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Purely cosmetic client-side rendering with no security relevance.

findings.title: Math.random selects a decoy organizer display name
findings.message: DECOY_ORGANIZER_NAMES[Math.floor(Math.random() * DECOY_ORGANIZER_NAMES.length)] picks a placeholder name for privacy masking.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Selection is for display obfuscation of an already-protected field, not a security token; predictability does not weaken any control.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.title: JSON.parse of a decrypted credential blob
findings.message: const decryptedKey = JSON.parse(...) parses a decrypted credential before persistence.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch and validate with a Zod schema for defense in depth.
findings.demotionReason: Input is server-side decrypted credential data (not raw client JSON), and the result is constrained to Prisma.InputJsonValue; downstream schema typing bounds the shape.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.title: Generic JSON.parse helper returns untyped data
findings.message: return JSON.parse(str) yields `any`, which can flow into typed sinks as a confused type.
findings.recommendation: Return `unknown` instead of implicit `any` and force callers to validate.
findings.demotionReason: This is a shared helper whose callers validate/parse results with Zod schemas before use; the helper itself performs no privileged action.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.sinkText: return await caller.publish(req.query as any /* Let tRPC handle this */);
findings.title: req.query cast to any before tRPC call
findings.message: return await caller.publish(req.query as any) bypasses static typing on the request query.
findings.recommendation: Replace the `as any` cast by parsing req.query with the procedure's input schema.
findings.demotionReason: The tRPC procedure performs its own input validation (Zod) on publish(), so the untyped value is re-validated server-side before any state change.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.title: Error message double-cast to an enum type
findings.message: if (Object.values(ErrorCode).includes(error.message as unknown as ErrorCode)) coerces a string to an enum for comparison.
findings.recommendation: Compare as a string against the enum's string values to avoid the unsafe cast.
findings.demotionReason: The cast is immediately guarded by an Object.values(...).includes() membership test, so an unexpected value simply fails the check rather than reaching a privileged path.

findings.title: API-key delete handler exported via defaultResponder
findings.message: export default defaultResponder(deleteHandler) exposes the [id] delete route.
findings.recommendation: Keep authorization in the route middleware; add a test asserting non-owners receive 403.
findings.demotionReason: Authorization for the /[id] route is enforced by the colocated _auth-middleware.ts (ownership/admin scoping) in the same route folder; defaultResponder is only the response/error wrapper, not the authorization boundary.

findings.title: API-key list handler exported via defaultResponder
findings.message: export default defaultResponder(getHandler) exposes the api-keys list endpoint.
findings.recommendation: No action required; retain the admin gate on cross-user queries.
findings.demotionReason: getHandler scopes results to the authenticated userId (admins may pass query.userId only when isSystemWideAdmin is true at api-keys/_get.ts:20), so records are not returned without an ownership/admin check.

findings.title: Attendee delete handler exported via defaultResponder
findings.message: export default defaultResponder(deleteHandler) exposes the attendee [id] delete route.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The colocated attendees/[id]/_auth-middleware.ts:15 constrains lookups to `{ id: query.id, booking: { userId } }`, enforcing that only the owning user can act on the attendee.

findings.title: API-key [id] method router dispatches without inline authz
findings.message: defaultResponder(async (req,res) => { return defaultHandler({...}) }) routes by HTTP method.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Each per-method handler (_get/_patch/_delete) is guarded by the route's _auth-middleware and handler-level ownership checks; the dispatcher itself performs no privileged data access.

findings.title: Embed posts messages to the parent with wildcard targetOrigin
findings.message: parent.postMessage({ originator:'CAL', ...data }, '*') broadcasts SDK lifecycle events to any parent document hosting the iframe.
findings.recommendation: Pin targetOrigin to the configured embed parent origin instead of '*' to prevent passive disclosure to unexpected ancestors.
findings.demotionReason: The embed is intentionally hosted by third-party parent pages, and the payload carries only non-sensitive lifecycle/UI events (dimensions, route, link clicks) with no credentials or PII; the inbound side validates message origin/shape.

findings.title: Custom routing page message rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: markdownToSafeHTMLClient(customPageMessage) }} injects user-authored markdown.
findings.recommendation: Keep using the sanitizer; periodically review its allowlist against new bypasses.
findings.demotionReason: The content is sanitized by markdownToSafeHTMLClient (an allowlist HTML sanitizer) before injection, neutralizing script/event-handler payloads.

findings.title: Team member bio rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: markdownToSafeHTML(member.bio) }} renders profile markdown.
findings.recommendation: No action required while the sanitizer remains in the path.
findings.demotionReason: member.bio passes through markdownToSafeHTML server-side sanitization before rendering, stripping active content.

findings.title: App description rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.message: <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: markdownToSafeHTML(source.content) }} /> renders app-store description markdown.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: source.content is sanitized via markdownToSafeHTML prior to injection.

findings.title: Inline script sets a page-status global
findings.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: `window.CalComPageStatus = '${pageStatus}'` }} writes a status flag.
findings.recommendation: Optionally JSON.stringify the value to harden against future non-constant inputs.
findings.demotionReason: pageStatus is a server-controlled enum/string constant (e.g. '200','404'), not user input, so no attacker-controlled data reaches the inline script.

findings.title: dayjs format string built from a browser-derived token
findings.message: dayjs(...).format(`${detectBrowserTimeFormat}, dddd DD MMMM YYYY`) embeds a locale time-format token in the format string.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: JavaScript has no C-style format-string semantics; dayjs.format only interprets date tokens, and detectBrowserTimeFormat is a constrained 12h/24h indicator, not attacker-controlled conversion specifiers.

findings.title: Composed dayjs format string for insights ranges
findings.message: return `${start.format(`${startFormat} , YYYY`)} - ${end.format(`${endFormat}, YYYY`)}` builds a date-range label.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: startFormat/endFormat are internally derived dayjs tokens; there is no externally controlled format specifier and no printf-style evaluation.

findings.categoryName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
findings.title: Request body spread into the booking creation payload
findings.message: { ...req.body } is spread into the object passed to booking creation, a mass-assignment surface where unexpected keys could ride along.
findings.recommendation: Construct the payload from explicitly named, schema-validated fields rather than spreading the raw body.
findings.demotionReason: The booking create path validates/whitelists fields via its Zod schema before persistence, and object spread copies own enumerable keys without invoking the prototype setter, so prototype pollution is not introduced here.

findings.categoryName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
findings.title: Request query spread into the cancel handler arguments
findings.message: { ...req.query, allRemainingBookings: req.query.allRemainingBookings === 'true' } merges raw query parameters.
findings.recommendation: Whitelist the specific query fields consumed by the handler.
findings.demotionReason: Query parameters are subsequently validated by the cancel-booking schema, and spread does not set the object prototype; only known, validated keys influence behavior.

findings.categoryName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
findings.title: Object.assign augments a request clone with server-derived fields
